Author(s): F. J. Qu et al. (DESI Collaboration) How galaxies expel gas is a big unknown and limits surveys in what they can measure. entry.title: Generation of perfect spatiotemporal acoustic vortices
entry.summary:
Author(s): Shuai Liu, Feng-Zhuang Liu, Hao Ge, Ming-Hui Lu, and Yan-Feng Chen Spatiotemporal acoustic vortices provide an intriguing route to encode transverse orbital angular momentum (OAM) in sound, but they have a fundamental constraint: Normally, their size grows with topological charge. This work overcomes that constraint by experimentally realizing perfect spatiotemporal acoustic vortices whose size remains nearly unchanged across different topological charges. The common vortex size also allows distinct OAM states to overlap and interfere on the same ring, producing programmable petal-like pressure patterns. These capabilities could facilitate acoustic multiplexing and detection, and structured-wave sensing and particle manipulation.

entry.title: Complex dynamical regimes of the Tayler-Spruit dynamo
entry.summary:
Author(s): Paul Barrère, Jérôme Guilet, Basile Gallet, and Raphaël Raynaud The amplification of large-scale magnetic fields via the Tayler-Spruit dynamo has been invoked to explain the slow rotation of stellar cores and the formation of magnetars. The existence of this mechanism has recently been proved via 3D MHD numerical simulations of a differentially rotating stably stratified fluid. Using the same setup, we show that the dynamo can produce a wide variety of magnetic field dynamics, including reversals and hemisphericity, by varying thermal stratification. In a fiducial simulation, we interpret the appearance of reversals as the result of the coupling of two large-scale magnetic modes with opposite equatorial symmetries by the symmetry breaking of the flow.

Author(s): Qiang Zou, Antik Sihi, Basu Dev Oli, Huimin Zhang, Mercè Roig, Daniel Agterberg, Michael Weinert, Lian Li, and Subhasish Mandal Here, the authors combine first-principles dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), epitaxial materials design, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, and scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy to show that superconductivity in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO3 is maximized at a magic FeSe4 tetrahedral angle. They demonstrate that strong electronic correlations, captured by DMFT, substantially enhance electron-phonon coupling within the FeSe layer and produce a superconducting dome. These findings reveal the microscopic origin of enhanced superconductivity and suggest a route for engineering higher-temperature superconductors.

entry.summary:
Author(s): Farell Keiser, Wentao Zhang, Dominik Johannesmann, Nicolas S. Beermann, Yuhao Meng, Hassan A. Hafez, Savio Fabretti, and Dmitry Turchinovich Zinc telluride (ZnTe) is widely used to generate and detect terahertz radiation with 800-nm laser pulses, yet its dielectric response at typical THz generation intensities remains unclear. Here, the authors show that two-photon absorption creates a transient free-carrier plasma strongly coupled to the lattice, modifying the THz dielectric function and markedly enhancing the 1.55-THz phonon resonance. These findings refine the physical description of THz generation in ZnTe and identify excitation-induced constraints on efficiency and bandwidth.

entry.summary:
Author(s): Kousuke Ishida, Hsiao-Yi Chen, Shumpei Seto, Hisashi Kotegawa, Ryoga Takahara, Yoichi Nii, Eiichi Matsuoka, Yusuke Wakabayashi, Clifford W. Hicks, Yusuke Nomura, and Yoshinori Onose CrAs undergoes a first-order helimagnetic transition accompanied by a huge lattice distortion whose microscopic mechanism remains unresolved. Here, the authors demonstrate through stress-strain measurements that the helimagnetic transition in CrAs is substantially more sensitive to uniaxial stress than to hydrostatic pressure. First-principles calculations reveal that this strong response originates from an entanglement between anisotropic strain and orbital-dependent correlations, showing that local correlations can drive nonlinear elastic responses in strongly correlated systems.

entry.title: Universal electron diffuse scattering in FCC alloys: A kinematic thermal diffuse-scattering analysis
entry.summary:
Author(s): Po-Cheng Kung, Tianyu Su, Elif Ertekin, Jian-Min Zuo, and Jessica Krogstad Chemical short-range order (CSRO) could be contributing significantly to properties of complex FCC alloys, but signals from thermal diffuse scattering (TDS) make its measurement challenging. Here, the authors establish a generalizable connection between characteristic TDS features and phonon dispersion relations in FCC materials. Simulations in pure FCC metals are consistent with features in medium-entropy and stainless steel experimental observations confirmed with temperature dependent measurements. As a result, they can identify scenarios in which TDS interferes with CSRO characterization via electron scattering techniques, and provide several strategies to enable robust identification of CSRO.

entry.title: Hidden magnetic complexity in the simple van der Waals ferromagnet ${\mathrm{Ce}}_{2}{\mathrm{Te}}_{5}$
entry.summary:
Author(s): Rajesh Tripathi, D. T. Adroja, C. Ritter, Leandro Liborio, Manuel dos Santos Dias, Leon Petit, D. Khalyavin, Yu Liu, T. Shiroka, M. Aouane, S. Langridge, S. Patil, and Eric D. Bauer Van der Waals magnets provide a platform for exploring how reduced dimensionality, competing interactions, and local electronic degrees of freedom shape magnetic order. Here, the authors uncover hidden complexity in Ce2Te5, a layered f-electron ferromagnet whose apparently simple magnetic ground state masks a richer microscopic landscape. Although the system develops a single long-range ferromagnetic structure, the two inequivalent Ce sites play markedly different roles in the ordered state, and subtle magnetic changes persist well below the ordering temperature. The combination of site-selective magnetism and strong single-ion anisotropy highlights how competing interactions can produce complex low-temperature behavior without generating additional long-range magnetic phases.

entry.summary:
Author(s): Alexandros T. Oratis, Matteo Camagna, Timo J. J. M. van Overveld, and Valeria Garbin Understanding mass transfer across particle-laden interfaces is crucial for the design of particle-stabilized emulsions for controlled release and chemical conversion. We show using experiments and theoretical modeling, that the particle layer generally has a negligible effect in the transport dynamics, irrespective of the particle size. Only at extreme surface coverages beyond the close-packing limit, is the particle layer expected to significantly hinder transport. These findings explain why diffusion can persist through particle-stabilized interfaces and pave the way to controlled transport in emulsion-based systems.

entry.title: Ab initio study of $^{7}\mathrm{Li}$ with coupled mass partitions
entry.summary:
Author(s): Jakub Herko, Konstantinos Kravvaris, Sofia Quaglioni, Petr Navrátil, Guillaume Hupin, and Mark A. Caprio A new capability of describing charge-exchange and transfer reactions by coupling different mass/charge partitions of the compound nucleus was developed within ab initio nuclear theory. We apply this capability to 7Li, employing the no-core shell model with continuum for the first time in a calculation that couples three mass/charge partitions, namely 4He + 3H, 6Li + n, and 6He + p, using a chiral nucleon-nucleon interaction as input. Specifically, we investigate the effect of interpartition coupling on the spectrum of 7Li and calculate cross sections for the 6Li(n,p)6He, 6He(p,n)6Li, and 6He(p,t)4He reactions. The results show that coupling the relevant mass/charge partitions is important for a consistent description of the 7Li spectrum and reaction cross sections, and offers a useful framework for interpreting existing data and guiding future measurements. This work also paves the way for calculations of transfer reactions relevant for fusion energy generation such as 6Li(n,t)4He.
[Phys. Rev. C 114, 044613] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026

entry.title: Gyrotropy from extrinsic geometry in twisted materials
entry.summary:
Author(s): Spenser Talkington and Eugene J. Mele Two-dimensional moiré materials feature widely tunable electronic structures. When these materials are illuminated by light, they exhibit optical gyrotropy in the form of circular dichroism and birefringence. Here, the authors show that this gyrotropy naturally decomposes into an intrinsic contribution due to interlayer electronic coupling and an extrinsic contribution due to the twisted embedding of the material in physical space. The authors conduct a general symmetry analysis applicable to moiré materials and identify regimes in which the intrinsic, and in which the extrinsic contributions dominate the gyrotropy. Finally, they apply the analysis to twisted bilayer graphene and twisted MoTe2.

entry.title: Nonlinear and added mass effects on the settling of particles with large to moderate density ratio in turbulence
entry.summary:
Author(s): A. Dejoan and R. Monchaux Using Eulerian-Lagrangian simulations, we investigate how particle-to-fluid density ratio influences solid particle settling in homogeneous turbulence, showing that lighter particles exhibit smaller settling rate velocities. While very heavy particles are governed by the sampled fluid velocity, moderately heavy particles decorrelate from the fluid under two-way coupling due to an added-mass force balancing the drag. Analysis reveals that increasing particle inertia broadens this velocity decorrelation, while nonlinear drag enhances departures from force equilibrium. Finally, we propose a method to account for particle self-disturbance and force-spreading operator issues in two-way coupling.

Author(s): U. Wahl, J. G. Correia, A. Costa, B. Biesmans, G. Magchiels, S. M. Tunhuma, A. Lamelas, A. Vantomme, and L. M. C. Pereira Understanding the properties of helium in diamond is crucial for geological dating and possible quantum applications. Here, the authors determine the lattice location of ion-implanted short-lived 6He in single-crystal diamond at temperatures from 30°C to 800°C using the β− emission channeling technique. 6He preferentially occupies tetrahedral interstitial sites. From the temperature dependence of the interstitial fraction, the migration energy of He is estimated at 1.63–2.89 eV, implying unbound interstitial helium is unstable in diamond over geological timescales, an important insight to be considered in He-based dating methods.
